I'm 66 this year, been farming these fields for 35 years. It's just me and my wife at home — our son works in a factory in the city and sends a bit of money back when he can, but we can't count on it. We have 10 mu of good flat land here in Quzhou. I only went to primary school, but I know this soil better than any professor. 

For the winter wheat, I plant in the first week of October, always have. I buy improved seed, about 35 jin per mu. Before planting, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's been my base for 20 years. When the wheat starts jointing around Qingming, I topdress about 30 jin of urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang uses more, but he has more money and his son helps full-time. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the ground is dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Pumping costs electricity money, so three times is my limit. I spray herbicide after planting, and if I see powdery mildew, I get fungicide. I hire the combine for harvest in early June — my back can't handle swinging a sickle anymore. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather is fair.

Summer maize goes in right after wheat comes out, mid-June, sometimes the very next morning. The window is tight, no time for deep plowing. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 3 jin per mu. I put about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow when planting. When the maize is knee-high, I side-dress about 20 jin of urea per mu — not as much as wheat, but enough. Maize doesn't need as much water, and the summer rains usually come, so I'll irrigate once, maybe at flowering if it's too dry. I spray herbicide, and if armyworms show up, I buy insecticide.

I do most work myself, though I pay for the combine and sometimes hire a neighbor with a tractor planter when I'm running late. My wife helps spread fertilizer and cook. We have to be careful with cash — she needs medicine, and we must keep some savings. I'd rather use a bit too much fertilizer than too little, because losing a crop would break us. But I also won't spend every yuan on inputs. That's how I've survived 35 years.
